title: Corollary
body_md:
{asymptotics of eigenspaces} 
For any Riemannian foliation on a closed manifold with a bundle-like metric and $k=2,3,\ldots,\infty$, the
assignment $h\mapsto\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_k^r(h)$ defines a continuous map from $[0,\infty)$ to the space of finite
dimensional linear subspaces of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r$ for all $r\geq0$. If $\dim\widehat E_1^r<\infty$, then this also
holds for $k=1$.

label: t:leafwise Hodge
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{t:leafwise Hodge}
For each $k\in\text{$\mathbb{Z}$}$, decomposition \eqref{e:leafwise Hodge} restricts to $W^k\Omega$; i.e.,
$$
W^k\Omega=\ker(\text{$\Delta$}_0\text{ in }W^k\Omega)\oplus\operatorname{cl}_k\left(\operatorname{im} d_{0,1}\right)
\oplus\operatorname{cl}_k\left(\operatorname{im}\delta_{0,-1}\right)
$$
as topological vector space. Thus \eqref{e:leafwise Hodge} also restricts to \text{$C^\infty$}\ differential forms; i.e.,
$$
\Omega=\ker\text{$\Delta$}_0\oplus\overline{\operatorname{im} d_{0,1}}
\oplus\overline{\operatorname{im}\delta_{0,-1}}
$$
with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology, where the bar denotes
\text{$C^\infty$}~closure in $\Omega$. In particular $\Pi$, $P$ and $Q$ preserve $\Omega$.

name: \'Alvarez-Kordyukov

label: t:H1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{t:H1}
We have:
\begin{itemize}

\item[$($i$)$] The operators $D_1$ and $\text{$\Delta$}_1$ are essentially
self-adjoint in $ L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$, and the operators $\widetilde{D}_1$ and $\widetilde{\text{$\Delta$}}_1$ are essentially
self-adjoint in $L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$. 

\item[$($ii$)$] The spectrums of ${\mathbf D}_1$, $\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1$, $\widetilde{{\mathbf D}}_1$ and
$\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Delta}}_1$ are discrete subsets of \text{$\mathbb{R}$}\ given by eigenvalues of finite multiplicity. 

\item[$($iii$)$] We have the Hodge type decompositions
\begin{align*}
 L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1&=\ker\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1\oplus\operatorname{im}{\mathbf d}_1\oplus\operatorname{im}\boldsymbol{\delta}_1\;,\\
 L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1&=\operatorname{im}\tilde{\mathbf d}_1\oplus\operatorname{im}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\delta}}_1\;,
\end{align*}
as Hilbert spaces with the $L^2$~norm, and moreover
\begin{gather*}
\ker\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1=\ker{\mathbf D}_1=\ker{\mathbf d}_1\cap\ker\boldsymbol{\delta}_1\;,\\
\operatorname{im}\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1=\operatorname{im}{\mathbf D}_1=\operatorname{im}{\mathbf d}_1\oplus\operatorname{im}\boldsymbol{\delta}_1\;,\\
\ker\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Delta}}_1=\ker\widetilde{{\mathbf D}}_1=0\;,\quad
\operatorname{im}\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1=\operatorname{im}{\mathbf D}_1=L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\;.
\end{gather*}
Furthermore the operators $\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1$ and
$\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Delta}}_1$ satisfy Garding type inequalities\footnote{\cite[Corollary~7.3]{AlvKordy1}.}.
Thus $\ker\boldsymbol{\Delta}_1=\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2$, and the above decompositions restrict to \text{$C^\infty$}~differential forms; i.e.,
\begin{align*}
{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1&=\ker\text{$\Delta$}_1\oplus\operatorname{im} d_1\oplus\operatorname{im}\delta_1\;,\\
\widetilde{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1&=\operatorname{im}\tilde d_1\oplus\operatorname{im}\tilde\delta_1\;,
\end{align*}
as topological vector spaces with the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology, as well as with the restriction
of the $L^2$~norm topology.

\item[$($iv$)$] The space ${\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_2$ is of finite dimension, and the
inclusion ${\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_2\hookrightarrow{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1$ induces isomorphisms
$${\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_2^{u,v}\stackrel{\cong}{\text{$\longrightarrow$}} 
H^u\left({\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1^{\cdot,v},d_1\right)
\cong H^u\left(\hat e_1^{\cdot,v}\right)
\cong H^u\left({\widehat E}_1^{\cdot,v}\right)\;.$$

\item[$($v$)$] We have $\tilde d_1^2=0$ and 
$H\left(\widetilde{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1,\tilde d_1\right)=0$.

\item[$($vi$)$] Each map $\widetilde{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1^{\cdot,v}\to\widetilde{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1^{\cdot,v}=\bar
o_1^{\cdot,v}\cong\bar0_1^{\cdot,v}$, defined by the canonical projection
$$
\overline{d_{0,1}\left(\Omega^{\cdot,v-1}\right)}
\oplus\overline{\delta_{0,-1}\left(\Omega^{\cdot,v}\right)}\text{$\longrightarrow$}
\overline{d_{0,1}\left(\Omega^{\cdot,v-1}\right)}/
d_{0,1}\left(\Omega^{\cdot,v-1}\right)\;,
$$
induces an isomorphism\footnote{The isomorphism
$H(\bar0_1)=0$ was originally shown  by X.~Masa \cite{Masa92}, as well as property~(vii), which
is a consequence.}
$$0=H^u\left(\widetilde{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1^{\cdot,v},d_1\right)
\cong H^u\left(\bar o_1^{\cdot,v}\right)\cong H^u\left(\bar0_1^{\cdot,v}\right)\;.$$

\item[$($vii$)$] All the following bigraded topological vector spaces are Hausdorff of finite
dimension and isomorphic to each other by maps that are either canonical or induced by the
projections $\pi_{u,v}$: $H({\hat e}_1)$, $H(e_1)$, $e_2$, $H({\widehat E}_1)$, $H(E_1)$ and
$E_2$.

\end{itemize}

title: Lemma
body_md:
{d10 P=P d10 P, ...}
The following properties are satisfied:
\begin{itemize}

\item[$($i$)$] We have
\begin{gather*}
\begin{alignat*}{3}
d_{1,0}P&=Pd_{1,0}P\;,&\qquad d_{1,0}\widetilde Q&=\widetilde Qd_{1,0}\widetilde Q\;,&\qquad
Qd_{1,0}&=Qd_{1,0}Q\;,\\
\widetilde Pd_{1,0}&=\widetilde Pd_{1,0}\widetilde P\;,&\qquad
\delta_{-1,0}Q&=Q\delta_{-1,0}Q\;,&\qquad
\delta_{-1,0}\widetilde P&=\widetilde P\delta_{-1,0}\widetilde P\;,
\end{alignat*}\\
P\delta_{-1,0}=P\delta_{-1,0}P\;,\qquad
\widetilde Q\delta_{-1,0}=\widetilde Q\delta_{-1,0}\widetilde Q\;.
\end{gather*}

\item[$($ii$)$] We have
$$
\widetilde Pd_{1,0}P=Qd_{1,0}\widetilde Q=\widetilde Q\delta_{-1,0}Q=
P\delta_{-1,0}\widetilde P=0\;.
$$

\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The equalities involving $d_{1,0}$ in property~(i) follow from~\eqref{e:d0,12=...} since 
$$
P(\Omega)=\overline{d_{0,1}(\Omega)}\;,\quad\widetilde Q(\Omega)=\ker d_{0,1}\;.
$$
The other equalities in property~(i) are obtained by taking adjoints, and
property~(ii) is a direct consequence of property~(i).

title: Lemma
body_md:
{H1} The following properties are satisfied:
\begin{itemize}

\item[$($i$)$] The following operators on $\Omega$ define bounded operators on
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$:
\begin{alignat*}{4}
&\widetilde\Pi d_{1,0}\Pi\;,&\qquad&\Pi d_{1,0}\widetilde\Pi\;,&\qquad&
\widetilde\Pi\delta_{-1,0}\Pi\;,&\qquad&\Pi\delta_{-1,0}\widetilde\Pi\;,\\
&\widetilde Qd_{1,0}Q\;,&\qquad&Pd_{1,0}\widetilde P\;,&\qquad&  
\widetilde P\delta_{-1,0}P\;,&\qquad&
Q\delta_{-1,0}\widetilde Q\;.
\end{alignat*}


\item[$($ii$)$] The following operators on $\Omega$ define bounded operators on
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ too:
\begin{alignat*}{4}
&\widetilde\Pi d\Pi\;,&\qquad&\Pi d\widetilde\Pi\;,&\qquad&
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v+1}d\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\;,&\qquad& 
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v-1}d\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\;,\\
&\widetilde\Pi\delta\Pi\;,&\qquad&\Pi\delta\widetilde\Pi\;,&\qquad&
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v+1}\delta\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\;,&\qquad&
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v-1}\delta\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\;.
\end{alignat*}

\item[$($iii$)$] We have 
\begin{alignat*}{2}
\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}_1&= L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\;,&\qquad
\operatorname{dom}\boldsymbol{\delta}_1&= L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\cap\operatorname{dom}\boldsymbol{\delta}\;,\\
\operatorname{dom}\tilde{{\mathbf d}}_1&= L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\;,&\qquad
\operatorname{dom}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\delta}}_1&= L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\cap\operatorname{dom}\boldsymbol{\delta}\;. 
\end{alignat*}

\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $D_\perp=d_{1,0}+\delta_{-1,0}$.
Then, by Remark~3.7 and the proof of Lemma~7.2 in \cite{AlvKordy1}, the
operators 
$$[D_\perp,\Pi]\;,\quad
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v-1}D_\perp\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\;,\quad
\left(\operatorname{id}-\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\right)D_\perp\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}$$
on $\Omega$ define bounded operators on $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. This easily yields
property~(i). Now properties~(ii) and~(iii) follows 
from property~(i) since $d_{2,-1}$
and $\delta_{-2,1}$ are of order zero, and
$d_{0,1}$ and $\delta_{0,-1}$ vanish on ${\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1$ and preserve each 
$\widetilde{\text{$\mathcal{H}$}}_1^{\cdot,v}$.

label: e:bfZ0+bfB0
title: Proof
body_md:
For $r=u+v$ we have
\begin{align}
\lefteqn{{\mathbf Z}_0^{u+1,v-1}+ {\mathbf B}_0^{u,v}}\notag\\
&=\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)
+{\mathbf d}\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u^{r-1}\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)\;,\quad\text{by \eqref{e:bfB0} and
\eqref{e:bfZ0}}\;,\notag\\
&=\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r
+{\mathbf d}\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u^{r-1}\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)\right)\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\;,\quad
\text{since}\quad\operatorname{im}{\mathbf d}\subset\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\;,\notag\\  
&=\left({\mathbf d}_{0,1}D^{u,v-1}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\;.\label{e:bfZ0+bfB0}
\end{align} 
Then 
$$Z_1^{u,v}\cap\left({\mathbf Z}_0^{u+1,v-1}+ {\mathbf B}_0^{u,v}\right)=
Z_0^{u+1,v-1}+B_0^{u,v}$$
by \eqref{e:B0}, \eqref{e:Z0} and \eqref{e:Z1}, and the result follows.

body_md:

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take any $\alpha\in D^{u,v}$. For $r=u+v$, there exists some
$\beta\in\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ such that $\alpha+\beta\in\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}$. So
$\pi_{u,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)$ is defined in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u,v}$. But 
$\pi_{u,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)={\mathbf d}_{0,1}\alpha$ because $\alpha+\beta\in\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u^r$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
{bfe1}
We have
$$
\pi_{u,v}\left({\mathbf Z}_1^{u,v}\right)=D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\;,\quad
\pi_{u,v}\left({\mathbf B}_0^{u,v}\right)={\mathbf d}_{0,1}D^{u,v-1}\;,
$$
and thus
$$
{\mathbf e}_1^{u,v}=\frac{D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}}{{\mathbf d}_{0,1}D^{u,v-1}}\;.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $r=u+v$, we have
\begin{alignat*}{2}
\pi_{u,v}\left({\mathbf Z}_1^{u,v}\right)
&=\pi_{u,v}\left(\left(\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\right)+
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)\;,&\qquad&\text{by \eqref{e:bfZ1}}\;,\\ 
&=\pi_{u,v}\left(\left(\left(D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\right)
+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)\;,&\qquad&\text{by \eqref{e:D}}\;,\\
&=D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\;,&&\\
\pi_{u,v}\left({\mathbf B}_0^{u,v}\right)
&=\pi_{u,v}\left({\mathbf d}\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u^{r-1}\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)\right)\;,&\qquad&
\text{by \eqref{e:bfB0}}\;,\\ 
&=\pi_{u,v}\left(\left({\mathbf d}_{0,1}D^{u,v-1}
+ \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}\right)\;,&\qquad&\text{by \eqref{e:D}}\;,\\
&={\mathbf d}_{0,1}D^{u,v-1}\;. &&
\end{alignat*}

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take any $\alpha\in D^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0\left(d_{0,1}\Omega^{u,v-1}\right)$,
and fix some $\beta\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ with $\alpha+\beta\in\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}$, where $r=u+v$. We
know that $\pi_{u+1,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)\in D^{u+1,v}$ by Lemma~\ref{l:bfe1}. On the other
hand, if $\bar{\mathbf d}_{0,1}$ and $\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}$ denote the extensions of
$d_{0,1}$ and $d_{1,0}$
to continuous maps
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}\to W^{-1}\Omega$, we have
$$\pi_{u+1,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)=\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\alpha+\bar{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\beta_1
\in\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\alpha+\bar{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u+1,v-1}\;,$$
where $\beta_1=\pi_{u+1,v-1}\beta\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u+1,v-1}$, and
$$
\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\alpha\in
\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\left(\operatorname{cl}_0\left(d_{0,1}\Omega^{u,v-1}\right)\right)
\subset\operatorname{cl}_{-1}\left(d_{0,1}\Omega^{u+1,v-1}\right)\;.
$$
Hence
$$\pi_{u+1,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)\in
D^{u+1,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_{-1}\left(d_{0,1}\Omega^{u+1,v-1}\right)
=D^{u+1,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0\left(d_{0,1}\Omega^{u+1,v-1}\right)$$
by Theorem~\ref{t:leafwise Hodge}. Therefore the result follows by Lemma~\ref{l:bfe1} and Corollary~\ref{c:barbfo1,hatbfe1}.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
{D Hodge}
We have
$$
D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}=
\left(D^{u,v}\cap  L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\right)
\oplus\left(D^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0\left(d_{0,1}\Omega^{u,v-1}\right)\right)
$$
as topological vector spaces, and moreover
$$
D^{u,v}\cap  L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1= L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}_1\;.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inclusion ``$\supset$'' of the first equality
is obvious, and the inclusion ``$\supset$'' of the second equality follows from
Lemma~\ref{l:H1}-(iii). 

To prove the inclusion ``$\subset$'' of the first equality,
by \eqref{e:leafwise Hodge} it is enough
to prove that $\Pi\alpha\in D^{u,v}$ for all $\alpha\in
D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}$. This obviously holds if we prove
$\Pi\alpha\in\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}_1$ for every such an $\alpha$ since the inclusion
``$\supset$'' of the second equality is already proved. This also proves the
inclusion ``$\subset$'' of the second equality by taking $\alpha\in  L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$. 

Thus take any $\alpha\in D^{u,v}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}$. Then there is some
$\beta\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ such that
$\alpha+\beta\in\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}$, where $r=u+v$. Write $\beta=\beta_1+\beta_2$ with $\beta_1\in
\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u+1,v-1}$ and $\beta_2\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+2}^r$. Thus, since
$\alpha\in\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}$, we get 
$$\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u+1,v}\ni\Pi\pi_{u+1,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)
=\Pi\left(\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\alpha+\bar{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\beta_1\right)
=\Pi\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\alpha\;.$$
Here we consider 
                                                                              
     
$\Pi$ and $\pi_{u+1,v}$ as bounded operators on $W^{-1}\Omega$. But
$$\Pi\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\alpha
=\Pi\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\Pi\alpha+\Pi\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}P\alpha$$
because $Q\alpha=0$, and 
$$\Pi\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}P\alpha=\Pi\widetilde{P}\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}P\alpha\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}$$
by Lemma~\ref{l:H1}-(i). Therefore $\Pi\bar{\mathbf d}_{1,0}\Pi\alpha\in\boldsymbol{\Omega}$, yielding
$\Pi\alpha\in\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}_1$ as desired.

title: Lemma
body_md:
{tilde D Hodge}
We have
$$\widetilde{D}^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0({\text{$\mathcal{B}$}}_v)=
\left(\widetilde{D}^{u,v}\cap L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1\right)
\oplus\left(D^{u+1,v-1}\cap\ker{\mathbf d}_{0,1}\right)$$
as topological vector spaces, and moreover

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inclusion ``$\supset$'' of the first equality is
obvious, and the inclusion ``$\supset$'' of the second equality follows from
Lemma~\ref{l:H1}-(iii). 

To prove the inclusion ``$\subset$'' of the first equality,
by \eqref{e:leafwise Hodge} it is enough
to prove that $\widetilde\Pi\alpha\in\widetilde{D}^{u,v}$ for all $\alpha\in
\widetilde{D}^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0({\text{$\mathcal{B}$}}_v)$. This obviously holds if we prove
$\widetilde\Pi\alpha\in\operatorname{dom}\tilde{\mathbf d}_1$ for every such an $\alpha$ since the
inclusion ``$\supset$'' of the second equality is already proved. This also
proves the inclusion ``$\subset$'' of the second equality by taking $\alpha\in
 L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$. 

Thus take any $\alpha\in \widetilde{D}^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0({\text{$\mathcal{B}$}}_v)$. Then there
is some
$\beta\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+2}^r$ such that
$\alpha+\beta\in\operatorname{dom}{\mathbf d}$, where $r=u+v$. Write $\alpha=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ with $\alpha_1\in
\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u,v}$ and $\alpha_2\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}^{u+1,v-1}$. So, since
$\alpha\in\operatorname{cl}_0({\text{$\mathcal{B}$}}_v)$ and
$\bar{\mathbf d}\beta\in\ker\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}$, where $\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}$ is
considered as a projection in $W^{-1}\Omega$, we get
$$\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}^{u+1,v}\ni
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}{\mathbf d}(\alpha+\beta)
=\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\alpha\;.$$ 
                                                                       
                                                                   
But
$$\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\alpha=
\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\alpha
+\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\Pi\alpha_2
+\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v-1}\alpha_2$$ because
$\alpha\in
\widetilde{D}^{u,v}\cap\operatorname{cl}_0({\text{$\mathcal{B}$}}_v)$, and
$$\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\Pi\alpha_2
+\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v-1}\alpha_2\in \boldsymbol{\Omega}$$
by Lemma~\ref{l:H1}-(ii). Therefore
$\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\bar{\mathbf d}\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\alpha\in\boldsymbol{\Omega}$, yielding
$\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}\alpha\in\operatorname{dom}\tilde{\mathbf d}_1$ as desired.

title: Lemma
body_md:
{Hilbert}
Let $L$ be a real complete metrizable topological vector space, and $V,W\subset L$ linear subspaces. If
$V\cap W=0$, $V$ is closed in $L$, and $W$ is closed in $V+W$, then $V+W=V\oplus W$ as topological
vector spaces.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have $(V+W)\cap\overline{W}=W$ since $W$ is closed in $V+W$, yielding
$V\cap\overline{W}=0$ because
$V\cap W=0$. So 
$V+\overline{W}=V\oplus\overline{W}$ as topological vector spaces because all spaces
involved are closed subspaces of $L$ (see for instance \cite[Corollary~3 of Theorem~2.1, Chapter~III,
page~78]{Schaefer}). Now the result follows easily.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
{ker d+Omega closed in Z+ker d+Omega}
For $u+v=r$, the space 
$(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ is a closed subspace of
${\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The space $\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}$ is closed in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ since ${\mathbf d}$ is a closed operator,
and thus so is its subspace ${\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}=\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u\cap(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})$. Hence
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}=V\oplus{\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}$
as Hilbert spaces, where $V$ is the orthogonal complement of ${\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}$ in 
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}$; in particular $V$ is closed in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ too. Obviously,
\begin{align*}
(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r&=V+{\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\;,\\
{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r
&=V+{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\;.
\end{align*}
On the other hand we clearly have
\begin{align*}
{\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r
&=\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u\cap\left((\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\;,\\
{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r
&=\boldsymbol{\Omega}_u\cap\left({\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\;,
\end{align*}
and thus ${\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ and ${\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ are
respectively closed in $(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$ and 
${\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r$. Therefore Lemma~\ref{l:Hilbert} yields
\begin{align*}
(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r
&=V\oplus\left({\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\;,\\
{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r
&=V\oplus\left({\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r\right)\;,
\end{align*}
as topological vector spaces, and the result follows.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
{technical difficulty}
In the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:ker d+Omega closed in Z+ker d+Omega}, the existence of $V$ so that
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}=V\oplus{\mathbf Z}_\infty^{u,v}$ as Hilbert spaces is the technical difficulty we were not
able to solve without using square integrable differential forms; that is, we do not know if 
$\Omega^r\cap\ker d=V\oplus Z_\infty^{u,v}$ as topological vector spaces for some subspace $V$. This is the
whole reason of introducing the $L^2$~spectral sequence in this paper. 

Also, observe that the formula of Gromov-Shubin uses square integrable
differential forms. Thus it can be more easily related to the 
$L^2$~spectral sequence than to the differentiable one. Though this is a minor problem that could be easily
solved in the setting of
\text{$C^\infty$}~differential forms.

there is some $C'_K>0$,

head: environment

label: e:ker rho
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $u+v=r$. The restriction $\rho_u^r:{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})\to X_u^r$ induces a
homomorphism 
$$
\bar\rho_u^r:\frac{{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,r-u}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})}{\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}}
\text{$\longrightarrow$}\frac{X_u^r}{\rho_u^r\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}\right)}\;.
$$
We clearly have
\begin{equation}\label{e:ker rho}
\ker\bar\rho_u^r=\frac{\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{u+1}^r+\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}\right)}
{\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d}}\;.
\end{equation}
So $\bar\rho_u^r$ induces a continuous linear isomorphism
$$
\frac{{\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})}
{{\mathbf Z}_{k-1}^{u+1,v-1}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})}
\stackrel{\cong}{\text{$\longrightarrow$}}
\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r=\frac{\rho_u^r\left({\mathbf Z}_k^{u,v}+(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})\right)}
{\rho_u^r(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^r\cap\ker{\mathbf d})}\;.
$$
Observe that $\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r$ is a Hausdorff topological vector space by 
Corollary~\ref{c:rho(ker d) closed in rho(Z+ker d)}, and thus $\left\|\cdot\right\|$ and $\left\|\cdot\right\|_h$ induce norms on
$\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r$ that will be also denoted by $\left\|\cdot\right\|$ and $\left\|\cdot\right\|_h$, respectively. By
\eqref{e:ker rho} and Corollary~\ref{c:L}, the homomorphism
$\bar\rho_u^r$ restricts to an injection
$\bar\rho_u^r:L_k^{u,v}\to\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r$.
Since $\rho_u^r$ is an orthogonal projection for any metric $g_h$, we easily get
\begin{equation}\label{e:rho}
\left\|\bar\rho_u^r\zeta\right\|_h\leq\left\|\zeta\right\|_h\quad\text{for all}\quad\zeta\in L_k^{u,v}\;.
\end{equation}
Here, we use the norm on $\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r$ in the left hand side of \eqref{e:rho}, and the
norm on $\boldsymbol{\Omega}/\ker{\mathbf d}$ in its right hand side. Observe that, by \eqref{e:| |h},
$$
h^{-q/2}h^u\left\|\omega\right\|\leq\left\|\omega\right\|_h\quad\text{for all}\quad
\omega\in X_u^r\quad\text{and}\quad 0<h\leq 1\;,
$$
yielding
\begin{equation}\label{e:im rho}
h^{-q/2}h^u\left\|\xi\right\|\leq\left\|\xi\right\|_h\quad\text{for all}\quad
\xi\in\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r\quad\text{and}\quad 0<h\leq 1\;.
\end{equation}
Moreover, since $K$ is of finite dimension, $\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r$ is Hausdorff, and the
restriction $\bar\rho_u^r:L_k^{u,v}\to\operatorname{im}\bar\rho_u^r$ is injective, we get the existence of
some $C'_K>0$ so that
\begin{equation}\label{e:C'K}
\left\|\zeta\right\|\leq C'_K\left\|\bar\rho_u^r\zeta\right\|\quad\text{for all}\quad\zeta\in K\;.
\end{equation}
So
\begin{alignat*}{2}
h^{-q/2}h^u\left\|\zeta\right\|&\leq C'_Kh^{-q/2}h^u\left\|\bar\rho_u^r\zeta\right\|\;,&&
\qquad\text{by~\eqref{e:C'K}}\;,\\
&\leq C'_K\left\|\bar\rho_u^r\zeta\right\|_h\;,&&\qquad\text{by~\eqref{e:im rho}}\;,\\
&\leq C'_K\left\|\zeta\right\|_h\;,&&\qquad\text{by~\eqref{e:rho}}\;,
\end{alignat*}
for all $\zeta\in K$ and $0<h\leq 1$ as desired.

title: Corollary
body_md:
{d zeta}
For each subspace $K\subset L_k^r$ of finite dimension 
there is some $C_K>0$, depending on $K$, such that
$$\left\|\bar{\mathbf d}\zeta\right\|_h\leq C_Kh^k\left\|\zeta\right\|_h$$
for all $\zeta\in K$ and $0<h\leq 1$.
head: environment

label: e:C''K
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $K$ is of finite dimension,
there is some constant $C''_K$, depending on $K$, so that 
\begin{equation}\label{e:C''K}
\left\|\bar{\mathbf d}\zeta\right\|\leq C''_K\left\|\zeta\right\|\qquad\text{for all}\quad\zeta\in
K\;.
\end{equation}

Because $L_k^r=\bigoplus_{u+v=r}L_k^{u,v}$, any finite
dimensional subspace $K\subset L_k^r$ is contained in the sum of finite dimensional
subspaces
$K^{u,v}\subset L_k^{u,v}$, $u+v=r$. Therefore we can assume $K$ is contained in some 
$L_k^{u,v}$ with $u+v=r$. Then, for
$\zeta\in K$ and $0<h\leq 1$, we have
\begin{alignat*}{2}
\left\|\bar{\mathbf d}\zeta\right\|_h&\leq h^{-q/2}h^{u+k}\left\|\bar{\mathbf d}\zeta\right\|\;,&&
\qquad\text{by Lemma~\ref{l:d zeta}}\;,\\
&\leq C''_Kh^{-q/2}h^{u+k}\left\|\zeta\right\|\;,&&\qquad\text{by \eqref{e:C''K}}\;,\\
&\leq C'_KC''_Kh^k\left\|\zeta\right\|_h\;,&&\qquad\text{by Lemma~\ref{l:C'K}}\;,
\end{alignat*}
and the result follows with $C_K=C'_KC''_K$.

label: e:ker and im of d1
title: Proof
body_md:
The result is proved by induction on $k$.
First, the case $k=1$ is trivial. 

Second, the kernel and the image of $d_1$ in $e_1^{u,v}$
respectively are
$z_2^{u,v}/b_0^{u,v}$ and
$b_1^{u,v}/b_0^{u,v}$, whose canonical projections in $\hat
e_1^{u,v}=z_1^{u,v}/\overline{b_0^{u,v}}$ are
\begin{equation}\label{e:ker and im of d1}
\frac{z_2^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}{\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}\;,\quad
\frac{b_1^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}{\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}\;,
\end{equation}
yielding the canonical isomorphism \eqref{e:hate1,ku,v=...} for $k=2$. Since the
isomorphism $e_2^{u,v}\cong\hat e_{1,2}^{u,v}$ is canonically defined, it corresponds to the
canonical map \eqref{e:zku,v/bk-1u,v to ...} for $k=2$.

Now assume the result holds for $k=\ell\geq2$ and we prove it for $k=\ell+1$. The kernel and the image
of $d_\ell$ in $e_\ell^{u,v}$ respectively are $z_{\ell+1}^{u,v}/b_{\ell-1}^{u,v}$ and
$b_\ell^{u,v}/b_{\ell-1}^{u,v}$, whose images by the canonical isomorphism
\eqref{e:zku,v/bk-1u,v to ...} for $k=\ell$ are
\begin{equation}\label{e:ker and im of dl}
\frac{z_{\ell+1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}{b_{\ell-1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}\;,\quad
\frac{b_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}{b_{\ell-1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}}\;.
\end{equation}
These spaces respectively correspond to the kernel and the image of $d_\ell$ in $\hat e_{1,\ell}^{u,v}$ by
\eqref{e:hate1,ku,v=...}, yielding  the canonical isomorphism \eqref{e:hate1,ku,v=...} for $k=\ell+1$.
Again, because the isomorphism $e_{\ell+1}^{u,v}\cong\hat e_{1,\ell+1}^{u,v}$ is canonically defined, it is
given by the canonical map \eqref{e:zku,v/bk-1u,v to ...} for $k=\ell+1$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
{calHk}
For $k\ge1$, $\Pi_k$ induces an isomorphism $\hat
e_{1,k}^{u,v}\stackrel{\cong}{\to}\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_k^{u,v}$, whose composition with the canonical
isomorphism $e_k^{u,v}\stackrel{\cong}{\to}\hat e_{1,k}^{u,v}$ is the above isomorphism

head: environment

label: e:zk+...=calHk oplus bk-1+...
title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that the first part of the statement means that we have an orthogonal decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{e:zk+...=calHk oplus bk-1+...}
z_k^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}=
\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_k^{u,v}\oplus\left(b_{k-1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)\;.
\end{equation}

Again the result follows by induction on $k$. We have an orthogonal decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{e:z1=calH1 oplus ...}
z_1^{u,v}=\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}\oplus\overline{b_0^{u,v}}
\end{equation}
by Theorem~\ref{t:leafwise Hodge}. Thus the isomorphism $\hat e_{1,1}=\hat
e_1^{u,v}\stackrel{\cong}{\to}\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}$ is induced by the orthogonal projection $\Pi_1$ onto
$\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$. On the other hand, the kernel and image of
$d_1$ in $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}$ respectively correspond by this isomorphism to the kernel and image of $d_1$ on
$\hat e_1^{u,v}$, which are respectively given by \eqref{e:ker and im of d1}. So the kernel and image of
$d_1$ in $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}$ are the orthogonal projections
$\Pi_1\left(z_2^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$ and
$\Pi_1\left(b_1^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$, respectively. Hence, by definition,
$\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2^{u,v}$ is the orthogonal complement of
$\Pi_1\left(b_1^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$ in
$\Pi_1\left(z_2^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$, which
is equal to the orthogonal complement of $b_1^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}$ in
$z_2^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}$ by \eqref{e:z1=calH1 oplus ...} since
$$\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\subset b_1^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}
\subset z_2^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\subset z_1^{u,v}\;.$$
Thus the result follows for $k=2$.

Now suppose the statement holds for $k=\ell\geq2$. Then, via the isomorphism $\hat
e_{1,\ell}^{u,v}\stackrel{\cong}{\to}\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ induced by $\Pi_\ell$, the kernel and image of
$d_\ell$ in $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ respectively correspond to the kernel and image of $d_\ell$ in $\hat
e_{1,\ell}^{u,v}$, which are given in \eqref{e:ker and im of dl}. So the kernel and image of
$d_\ell$ in $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ are the orthogonal projections
$\Pi_\ell\left(z_{\ell+1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$ and
$\Pi_\ell\left(b_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$, respectively. Hence, by definition,
$\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_{\ell+1}^{u,v}$ is the orthogonal complement of
$\Pi_\ell\left(b_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$ in
$\Pi_\ell\left(z_{\ell+1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)$, which
is equal to the orthogonal complement of $b_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}$ in
$z_{\ell+1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}$ by \eqref{e:zk+...=calHk oplus bk-1+...} for $k=\ell$ since
$$b_{\ell-1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\subset b_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}
\subset z_{\ell+1}^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\subset z_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\;.$$
Thus the result follows for $k=\ell+1$.

\begin{align*}
\Pi_2\pi_{u+2,v-2}d\tilde d_1\beta&=
\Pi_2\left(d_{2,-1}\left(d_{1,0}\beta'+d_{0,1}\beta''\right)
+d_{1,0}Q\left(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta''\right)\right)\\
&=\Pi_2\left(\left(d_{2,-1}d_{1,0}+d_{1,0}d_{2,-1}\right)\beta'
+\left(d_{2,-1}d_{0,1}+d_{1,0}^2\right)\beta''\right)\\
&\quad -\Pi_2d_{1,0}\Pi\left(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta''\right)
-\Pi_2d_{1,0}P\left(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta''\right)\\
&=\text{}-\Pi_2d_1\Pi\left(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta''\right)
-\Pi_2Pd_{1,0}P\left(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta''\right)\\
&=0
\end{align*}
by \eqref{e:d0,12=...}, Lemma~\ref{l:d10 P=P d10 P, ...} and because $\Pi_2d_{0,1}=\Pi_2d_1=\Pi_2P=0$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
{Pi2 piu+2,v-1 d}
Let $\alpha_i$ be a sequence in $\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}$ such that
$\tilde d_1\alpha_i\to0$ strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Then 
$$\Pi_2\pi_{u+2,v-1}d\alpha_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0$$
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the image of $\tilde d_1$ is closed and equal to its kernel, the hypothesis implies the
existence of a sequence
$\beta_i\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u-1,v}$ such that $\alpha_i+\tilde d_1\beta_i\to0$ strongly in
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. On the other hand we have
\begin{align*}
\Pi_2\pi_{u+2,v-1}d&=\Pi_2d_{2,-1}\pi_{u,v}+\Pi_2d_{1,0}\pi_{u+1,v-1}\\
&=\Pi_2d_{2,-1}\pi_{u,v}+\Pi_2\Pi d_{1,0}Q\pi_{u+1,v-1}
\end{align*}
on $\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}$, and thus the operator
$\Pi_2\pi_{u+2,v-1}d:\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}\to\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2^{u+2,v-1}$ is bounded because
$d_{2,-1}$ and $\Pi d_{1,0}Q$ are bounded operators in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ by Lemma~\ref{l:H1}. Therefore
$$
\Pi_2\pi_{u+2,v-1}d(\alpha_i+\tilde d_1\beta_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
$$
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Then the result follows directly from Lemma~\ref{l:Pi2 piu+2,v-2 d tilded1 beta}.

label: e:Pi2 d10 Q alphai lar gamma
title: Proof
body_md:
In this case we have $\gamma\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2^{u+2,v-1}$ and $\alpha_i\in\Omega^{u+1,v-1}$, which satisfy
$$
d_{0,1}\alpha_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
Qd_{1,0}\alpha_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
\Pi_2d_{1,0}\alpha_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}\gamma
$$
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Since 
$$\Pi d_{1,0}\Pi\alpha_i=d_1\Pi\alpha_i\perp\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2^{u+2,v-1}\;,$$
we get $\Pi_2d_{1,0}\widetilde\Pi\alpha_i\to\gamma$ strongly in
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. But $\Pi_2d_{1,0}P\alpha_i=\Pi_2Pd_{1,0}P\alpha_i=0$ by Lemma~\ref{l:d10 P=P d10 P, ...}, and
thus we get 
\begin{equation}\label{e:Pi2 d10 Q alphai lar gamma}
\Pi_2\pi_{u+2,v-1} dQ\alpha_i=\Pi_2 d_{1,0}Q\alpha_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}\gamma
\end{equation}
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Now observe that
$Q\alpha_i\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v}$, and 
$$
\tilde d_1Q\alpha_i=\widetilde\Pi_{u+1,v}dQ\alpha_i
=d_{0,1}Q\alpha_i+Qd_{1,0}Q\alpha_i
=d_{0,1}\alpha_i+Qd_{1,0}\alpha_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
$$
because $d_{0,1}Q=d_{0,1}$ and by Lemma~\ref{l:d10 P=P d10 P, ...}. Then the
result follows by \eqref{e:Pi2 d10 Q alphai lar gamma} and Lemma~\ref{l:Pi2 piu+2,v-1 d}.

title: Proof
body_md:
First, we check that the assignment $\omega\mapsto\gamma$, under the conditions in
the statement, defines a map $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}\to\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$---observe that, if such a map
is well defined, it is obviously linear---. Suppose there is another
$\gamma'\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$ and another sequence
$\alpha'_i\in\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}$ such that
\begin{gather*}
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d\alpha'_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0<a<\ell\;,\\
\bar Q_{\ell-2}\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d\alpha'_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
\Pi_\ell\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d\alpha'_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}\gamma'
\end{gather*}
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Then the sequence $\alpha_i-\alpha'_i\in\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}$ satisfies
\begin{gather*}
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d(\alpha_i-\alpha'_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0<a<\ell\;,\\
\bar Q_{\ell-2}\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\alpha_i-\alpha'_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
\Pi_\ell\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\alpha_i-\alpha'_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}\gamma-\gamma'
\end{gather*}
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Therefore $\gamma=\gamma'$ by Lemma~\ref{l:dk=0 in calHk} for the case $k=\ell$.

Second, we prove that the above map $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}\to\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$ is
$d_\ell$; i.e., for each $\omega\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$, we prove the existence of a sequence
$\alpha_i\in\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}$ such that
\begin{gather}
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0\leq a<\ell\;,
\label{e:piu+a,v-a+1 d(omega+alphai) lar0}\\
\bar Q_{\ell-2}\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,
\label{e:Ql-2 piu+l,v-l+1 d(omega+alphai) lar0}\\
\Pi_\ell\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$} d_\ell\omega
\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}\label{e:Pil piu+l,v-l+1 d(omega+alphai) lar0}
\end{gather}
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. According to \eqref{e:summarize}, for each
$\omega\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ there is a sequence
$\omega_i\in z_\ell^{u,v}$ converging to $\omega$ with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology and such that
$\omega$ and all the $\omega_i$ define the same class $\hat\zeta\in\hat e_{1,\ell}^{u,v}$; thus
all the $\omega_i$ define the same class $\zeta\in e_\ell^{u,v}$. By definition of
$z_\ell^{u,v}$, there is another sequence $\alpha_i\in\Omega^{u+v}_{u+1}$ such that
$\omega_i+\alpha_i\in Z_\ell^{u,v}$. So all the
$\omega_i+\alpha_i$ define the same class
$\xi\in E_\ell^{u,v}$, and the class $d_\ell\xi\in E_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$ is defined by
any of the forms $d(\omega_i+\alpha_i)\in Z_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$. Thus 
$$
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d(\omega_i+\alpha_i)=0\;,\quad 0\leq a<\ell\;,
$$
and any of the forms
$$
\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega_i+\alpha_i)\in z_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}
$$
define the class $d_\ell\zeta\in e_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$ as well as the class
$d_\ell\hat\zeta\in\hat e_{1,\ell}^{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}$, yielding 
\begin{gather*}
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d(\omega_i+\alpha_i)=0\;,\quad 0\leq a<\ell\;,\\
\bar Q_{\ell-2}\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega_i+\alpha_i)=0\;,\\
\Pi_\ell\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega_i+\alpha_i)=d_\ell\omega\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+\ell,v-\ell-1}
\end{gather*}
independently of $i$. Then~\eqref{e:piu+a,v-a+1
d(omega+alphai) lar0}--\eqref{e:Pil piu+l,v-l+1 d(omega+alphai) lar0} follow by the \text{$C^\infty$}~convergence
$\omega_i\to\omega$, as desired. 

Finally we prove the last part of the statement.
Observe that, in fact, the above arguments yield \text{$C^\infty$}~convergence in \eqref{e:piu+a,v-a+1
d(omega+alphai) lar0}--\eqref{e:Pil piu+l,v-l+1 d(omega+alphai) lar0}, and also the \text{$C^\infty$}~convergence
$$
\bar Q_{\ell-1}\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;.
$$
For each $i$, take $\sigma_i^1\in Q_1(\Omega^{u+\ell-1,v-\ell+1})$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{e:Pi1 d1,0 sigmai1 = P1 ...}
\Pi_1d_{1,0}\sigma_i^1=P_1\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\;,
\end{equation}
and take $\sigma_i^0\in Q_0(\Omega^{u+\ell,v-\ell})$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{e:d0,1 sigmai0 + P0 d1,0 sigmai1 - P0... lar0}
d_{0,1}\sigma_i^0+P_0d_{1,0}\sigma_i^1
-P_0\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
\end{equation}
with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology. If $\ell>2$, for each $i$ and $m=2,\ldots,\ell-1$ take some
$\sigma_i^m\in Q_m(\Omega^{u+\ell-m,v-\ell+m})$ such that
$$
d_m\sigma_i^m=P_m\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\;.
$$
By Proposition~\ref{p:dk in calHk} for $k<\ell$ there are
sequences $\tau_{i,j}^m\in\Omega_{u+\ell-m+1}^{u+v}$ such that
\begin{gather*}
\pi_{u+\ell-m+a,v-\ell+m-a+1}d(\sigma_i^m+\tau_{i,j}^m)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0<a<m\;,\\
\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\sigma_i^m+\tau_{i,j}^m)\text{$\longrightarrow$} P_m\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)
\end{gather*}
with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology in $\Omega$. Then, for each $i,m$ we can clearly choose $j$
depending on $i,m$ so that $\tau_i^m=\tau_{i,j}^m$ satisfies
\begin{gather}
\pi_{u+\ell-m+a,v-\ell+m-a+1}d(\sigma_i^m+\tau_i^m)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0<a<m\;,
\label{e:piu+l-m+a,v-l+m-a+1 d(sigmaim + tauim) lar0}\\
\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\sigma_i^m+\tau_i^m)
-P_m\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega+\alpha_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
\label{e:piu+l,v-l+1 d(sigmaim + tauim) - Pm ... lar0}
\end{gather}
with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology. Let 
$$
\beta_i=\alpha_i-\sigma_i^0-\sigma_i^1-\sum_{m=2}^{\ell-1}(\sigma_i^m+\tau_i^m)
\in\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}\;,
$$
where the last term does not show up if $\ell=2$. 
From~\eqref{e:Pi1 d1,0 sigmai1 = P1 ...}--\eqref{e:piu+l,v-l+1 d(sigmaim + tauim) - Pm ... lar0} we get
\begin{gather*}
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d(\omega_i+\beta_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0\leq a<\ell\;,\\
\pi_{u+\ell,v-\ell+1}d(\omega_i+\beta_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$} d_\ell\omega
\end{gather*}
with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology in $\Omega$, and the proof is finished.

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the following subspaces of $\Omega^{u+v}$:
\begin{gather*}
\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_\ell^{u,v}=Z_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{B_0^{u,v}}+\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}
=\left(z_\ell^{u,v}+\overline{b_0^{u,v}}\right)\oplus\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}\;,\\
\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{u,v}=B_0^{u,v}+\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}=b_0^{u,v}\oplus\Omega_{u+1}^{u+v}\;.
\end{gather*}
First, observe that each $\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ is the orthogonal complement of 
$\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_{\ell-1}^{u+\ell,v-\ell}$ in $\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{u,v}}$, and thus
$\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$ is the orthogonal complement of
$\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_{\ell-1}^{\cdot,v-\ell}=\bigoplus_a\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_\ell^{a,v-\ell}$ in
$\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{\cdot,v}}=\bigoplus_a\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{a,v}}$. So the inclusion
$\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}\hookrightarrow\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{\cdot,v}}$ induces an isomorphism
of topological vector spaces
\begin{equation}\label{e:widetilde calHl.,v=overline calB.,v/calAl-1.,v-l}
\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}\stackrel{\cong}{\text{$\longrightarrow$}}
\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{\cdot,v}}/\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_{\ell-1}^{\cdot,v-\ell}
\end{equation}
whose inverse is induced by the orthogonal projection
$\widetilde\Pi_{\cdot,v}:\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{\cdot,v}}\to\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$. Second, 
observe that both $\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{u,v}}$ and $\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_{\ell-1}^{\cdot,v-\ell}$ are subcomplexes of
$(\Omega,d)$. Moreover $\tilde d_\ell$ in $\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$ clearly corresponds
to the differential map in the quotient complex
$\overline{\text{$\mathcal{B}$}^{\cdot,v}}/\text{$\mathcal{A}$}_{\ell-1}^{\cdot,v-\ell}$ via \eqref{e:widetilde calHl.,v=overline
calB.,v/calAl-1.,v-l}, and the result follows.

title: Lemma
body_md:
{Pil+1 piu+l,v-l d tildePil d beta}
For any 
$$
\beta\in\bigoplus_{a<\ell}\Omega^{u-1+a,v-a}+\bar Q_{\ell-1}(\Omega^{u-1+\ell,v-\ell})
$$
we have 
$$
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d\beta=0\;.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the expression
\begin{multline*}
\bigoplus_{a<\ell}\Omega^{u-1+a,v-a}+\bar Q_{\ell-1}(\Omega^{u-1+\ell,v-\ell})\\
=\bigoplus_{a<\ell}\Omega^{u-1+a,v-a}
+\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u+\ell-2,v-\ell+1}+(Q_1+\cdots+Q_{\ell-1})(\Omega^{u+\ell-1,v-\ell})
\end{multline*}
it is enough to consider the following three cases. First, assume
$\beta\in\bigoplus_{a<\ell}\Omega^{u-1+a,v-a}$ and let $\beta'=\pi_{u+\ell-2,v-\ell+1}\beta$. We
clearly have
$$
(d-\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d)\beta=(\operatorname{id}-\bar Q_{\ell-1})d_{2,-1}\beta'
=(Q_\ell+\Pi_{\ell+1}+\bar P_\ell)d_{2,-1}\beta'\;,
$$
yielding
\begin{align*}
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d\beta
&=-\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(Q_\ell+\Pi_{\ell+1}
+\bar P_\ell)d_{2,-1}\beta'\\
&=-\Pi_{\ell+1}d_{1,0}(Q_\ell+\Pi_{\ell+1}+\bar P_\ell)d_{2,-1}\beta'\\
&=-\Pi_{\ell+1}d_1(Q_\ell+\Pi_{\ell+1}+P_1+\cdots+P_\ell)d_{2,-1}\beta'\\
&\quad -\Pi_{\ell+1}d_{1,0}P_0d_{2,-1}\beta'\\
&=0
\end{align*}
by Lemma~\ref{l:d10 P=P d10 P, ...}, and because $\Pi_{\ell+1}d_1=0$ and $\Pi_{\ell+1}P_0=0$.

Second, suppose $\beta\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u+\ell-2,v-\ell+1}$ and write $\beta=\beta'+\beta''$
with 
$$
\beta'\in P_0(\Omega^{u+\ell-2,v-\ell+1})\;,\quad\beta''\in Q_0(\Omega^{u+\ell-1,v-\ell})\;.
$$
We clearly have
$$
(\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d-\tilde d_1)\beta=(\tilde d_\ell-\tilde
d_1)\beta=(Q_1+\cdots+Q_{\ell-1})(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta'')\;,
$$
yielding
\begin{align*}
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d\beta
&=\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\tilde d_1\beta\\
&\quad +\Pi_{\ell+1}d_{1,0}(Q_1+\cdots+Q_{\ell-1})(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta'')\\
&=\Pi_{\ell+1}\Pi_2\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\tilde d_1\beta\\
&\quad +\Pi_{\ell+1}d_1(Q_1+\cdots+Q_{\ell-1})(d_{2,-1}\beta'+d_{1,0}\beta'')\\
&=0
\end{align*}
by Lemma~\ref{l:Pi2 piu+2,v-2 d tilded1 beta}.

Third, assume $\beta\in(Q_1+\cdots+Q_{\ell-1})(\Omega^{u+\ell-1,v-\ell})$, which is contained in
$\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u+\ell-1,v-\ell}$. Then the result follows
because $\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d=\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d_1$ on
$\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{\cdot,v-\ell}$, and
$$
d_1\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{\cdot,v-\ell}\subset
P_1(\Omega^{\cdot,v-\ell})\perp\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}\;.
$$

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\alpha=\alpha'+\alpha''+\alpha'''$
with $\alpha'\in P_0(\Omega^{u,v})$, $\alpha''\in\Omega^{u+1,v-1}$ and
$$
\alpha'''\in\bigoplus_{2\leq a<\ell}\Omega^{u+a,v-a}\oplus\bar
Q_{\ell-1}(\Omega^{u+\ell,v-\ell})\;.
$$

Observe that $\alpha'+Q_0\alpha''\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{\cdot,v}$. Since $\tilde d_\ell\alpha=0$
and $\tilde d_1=\widetilde\Pi_{1;\cdot,v}\tilde d_\ell$ on $\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{\cdot,v}$, we have
$\tilde d_1(\alpha'+Q_0\alpha'')=0$. Thus there is some $\beta\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u-1,v}$ with
$\tilde d_1\beta=\alpha'+Q_0\alpha''$ because $H(\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{\cdot,v},\tilde d_1)=0$. Then
$\alpha-\tilde d_\ell\beta\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ satisfies
$$
\pi_{u,v}(\alpha-\tilde d_\ell\beta)=Q_0\pi_{u+1,v-1}(\alpha-\tilde d_\ell\beta)=0\;,
$$
and moreover
$$
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\alpha
=\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(\alpha-\tilde d_\ell\beta)
$$
by Lemma~\ref{l:Pil+1 piu+l,v-l d tildePil d beta}. Therefore we can assume $\alpha'+Q_0\alpha''=0$, and
thus $\alpha'=Q_0\alpha''=0$. With this assumption, it follows that
$\alpha''=(\Pi_1+P_0)\alpha''$ and
$$
d_1\Pi_1\alpha''=\Pi_1d_{1,0}\Pi_1\alpha''=\Pi_1d_{1,0}\alpha''=\Pi_1\pi_{u+2,v-1}d\alpha
=\Pi_1\pi_{u+2,v-1}\tilde d_\ell\alpha=0
$$
by Lemma~\ref{l:d10 P=P d10 P, ...}, yielding $Q_1\alpha''=0$.

Take a sequence
$$
\phi_i\in Q_0(\Omega^{u+1,v-2})\subset\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u-1,v}
$$
such that $d_{0,1}\phi_i$ is \text{$C^\infty$}~convergent to $P_0\alpha''$.
Then the sequence $\alpha-\tilde d_\ell\phi_i\in\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u,v}$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\alpha
&=\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(\alpha-\tilde d_\ell\phi_i)\\
&\text{$\longrightarrow$}\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(\Pi_1\alpha''+\alpha''')
\end{align*}
by Lemma~\ref{l:Pil+1 piu+l,v-l d tildePil d beta}. So
$$
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\alpha
=\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(\Pi_1\alpha''+\alpha''')\;,
$$
and thus we can also assume $P_0\alpha''=0$.


For each $k=1,\dots,\ell-1$ there is some
$\sigma^k\in Q_k(\Omega^{u-k+1,v+k-2})$
with $d_k\sigma^k=P_k\alpha''$. As above, from the existence of such a $\sigma^1$ we
can assume $P_1\alpha''=0$ by Lemma~\ref{l:Pil+1 piu+l,v-l d tildePil d beta} since
$d_1=\pi_{u,v-1}\Pi_1\tilde d_\ell$ on
$\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^{u,v-1}$. If $\ell>2$, by Proposition~\ref{p:dk in calHk} for $k=2,\ldots,\ell-1$ there is a sequence
$\tau^k_i\in\Omega^{u+v-1}_{u-m+2}$ such that
\begin{gather*}
\pi_{u-k+a+1,v+k-a-1}d(\sigma^k+\tau^k_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad 0<a<k\;,\\
\pi_{u+1,v-1}d(\sigma^k+\tau^k_i)\text{$\longrightarrow$} P_k\alpha''
\end{gather*}
with respect to the \text{$C^\infty$}~topology in $\Omega$. We can thus suppose $P_k\alpha''=0$ for
such a $k$ because 
$$
\Pi_{\ell+1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}d(\sigma^k+\tau^k_i)=0
$$
by Lemma~\ref{l:Pil+1 piu+l,v-l d tildePil d beta}. Therefore 
\begin{equation}\label{e:alpha'' in ...}
\alpha''\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+1,v-1}\oplus\bigoplus_{k=2}^{\ell-1}Q_k(\Omega^{u+1,v-1})\;,
\end{equation}
where the last term does not show up if $\ell=2$.

Now the condition $\tilde d_\ell\alpha=0$ can be written as
\begin{equation}\label{e:d(alpha''+alpha''')}
\pi_{u+1+a,v-a}d(\alpha''+\alpha''')
=\bar Q_{\ell-1}\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(\alpha''+\alpha''')=0\;,\quad0<a<\ell\;.
\end{equation}
Observe that~\eqref{e:d(alpha''+alpha''')} summarizes the conditions of the first part of Proposition~\ref{p:dk in calHk} for
$k=2,\dots,\ell$, with $\omega=\alpha''$, the constant sequence $\alpha_i=\alpha'''$, and 
$\gamma=0$ if $2\leq k<\ell$. Since $\alpha''\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2^{u+1,v-1}$ by~\eqref{e:alpha'' in ...}, we
get inductively on $k=2,\dots,\ell-1$ that $\alpha''\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_k^{u+1,v-1}$ and $d_k\alpha''=0$
by~\eqref{e:alpha'' in ...},~\eqref{e:d(alpha''+alpha''')} and Proposition~\ref{p:dk in calHk}. Hence
$\alpha''\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{u+1,v-1}$ by~\eqref{e:alpha'' in ...},
and thus
$$
\Pi_\ell\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d\alpha=\Pi_\ell\pi_{u+\ell+1,v-\ell}d(\alpha''+\alpha''')
=d_\ell\alpha''\perp\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_{\ell+1}
$$
by~\eqref{e:d(alpha''+alpha''')} and Proposition~\ref{p:dk in calHk} for $k=\ell$, and the result follows.

title: Proof

By Theorem~2.2 in \cite{Chernoff}, $D=d+\delta$ is essentially
self-adjoint in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. Then, by using e.g. Lemma~XII.1.6--(c) in
\cite{DunfordSchwartz}, so is $\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v} D\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}$
because $\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}$ is a bounded self-adjoint
operator on $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. But $\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v} D\widetilde\Pi_{\ell;\cdot,v}$ is equal
to $\widetilde D_\ell$ in $L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$ and vanishes in its orthogonal
complement. Hence $\widetilde D_\ell$ is essentially self-adjoint.

&=\widetilde P_0(\delta_{-1,0}+\delta_{-2,1}\pi_{\cdot,v-1})
+\delta_{-2,1}\pi_{\cdot,v}\\
&\quad +(\Pi_\ell+\bar
P_{\ell-1})(d_{1,0}\pi_{\cdot,v-\ell}+d_{2,-1}\pi_{\cdot,v-\ell+1})\\ 
&\quad +d_{2,-1}\pi_{\cdot,v-\ell}\;.

But

P_0d_{1,0}\pi_{\cdot,v-\ell}=P_0d_{1,0}\widetilde P_0\pi_{\cdot,v-\ell}

on $\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$. Then the result follows by Lemma~\ref{l:H1}-(i).

title: Corollary
body_md:
{Hodge theory for tildecalHl}
The Hilbert space $L^2\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$ has a complete
orthonormal system $\{\phi_i : i=1,2,\ldots\}\subset\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}$,
consisting of eigenvectors of $\widetilde\text{$\Delta$}_\ell$, so that
the corresponding eigenvalues satisfy
$0\leq\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ with $\lambda_i\uparrow\infty$
if $\dim\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}=\infty$; thus all of these eigenvalues have finite
multiplicity. We also have the orthogonal decomposition
$$
\widetilde\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_\ell^{\cdot,v}=(\ker\tilde d_\ell\cap\ker\tilde\delta_\ell)\oplus
\operatorname{im}\tilde d_\ell\oplus\operatorname{im}\tilde\delta_\ell\;,
$$
with
\begin{align*}
\ker\widetilde\text{$\Delta$}_\ell&=\ker\tilde d_\ell\cap\ker\tilde\delta_\ell\;,\\
\operatorname{im}\widetilde\text{$\Delta$}_\ell&=\operatorname{im}\tilde d_\ell\oplus\operatorname{im}\tilde\delta_\ell\;,\\
\ker d_\ell&=(\ker\tilde d_\ell\cap\ker\tilde\delta_\ell)\oplus\operatorname{im}\tilde d_\ell\;,\\
\ker\delta_\ell&=(\ker\tilde d_\ell\cap\ker\tilde\delta_\ell)\oplus\operatorname{im}\tilde\delta_\ell\;.
\end{align*}

title: Lemma
body_md:

head: environment
name: \'Alvarez-Kordyukov

title: Proposition
body_md:
{Delta h}
There is some $C>0$ such that\footnote{Recall that, for self-adjoint operators $A,B$ in a Hilbert space
$H$, the inequality $A\leq B$ is defined in the sense of quadratic forms: $\langle Au,u\rangle\leq\langle
Bu,u\rangle$ for all $u\in H$.}
$$
\text{$\Delta$}_h\geq \frac{1}{2}\text{$\Delta$}_0+\frac{1}{2}h^2\text{$\Delta$}_\perp-Ch^2
$$
for $h$ small enough.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the operators $B,F$ given by Lemma~\ref{l:Dperp D0+D0 Dperp} and \eqref{e:D h}.
Since $B,F$ are of order zero, there is
some $C'>0$ such that
$B^\ast B,F^2\leq C'$. Because $D_0$ is symmetric, we get
\begin{align*}
h\,|\langle(BD_0+D_0B^\ast)\omega,\omega\rangle|
&\leq 2h\,|\langle D_0\omega,B\omega\rangle|\\
&\leq 2h\,\|D_0\omega\|\,\|B\omega\|\\
&\leq\frac{1}{4}\,\|D_0\omega\|^2+4h^2\,\|B\omega\|^2\\
&=2\left\langle\left(\frac{1}{4}\text{$\Delta$}_0+4h^2B^\ast B\right)\omega,\omega\right\rangle
\end{align*}
for all $\omega\in\Omega$, yielding
$$h\,|BD_0+D_0B^\ast|\leq\text{$\Delta$}_0+h^2B^\ast B\leq\text{$\Delta$}_0+C'h^2.$$
Similarly we get
$$\begin{array}{c}
\left|FD_0+D_0F\right|\leq\text{$\Delta$}_0+F^2\leq\text{$\Delta$}_0+C'\;,\\[6pt]
\left|FD_\perp+D_\perp F\right|\leq\text{$\Delta$}_\perp+F^2\leq\text{$\Delta$}_0+C'\;.
\end{array}$$
Therefore, from \eqref{e:D h} and Lemma~\ref{l:Dperp D0+D0 Dperp} we get
\begin{align*}
\text{$\Delta$}_h&=\text{$\Delta$}_0+h^2\text{$\Delta$}_\perp+h^4F^2+h(BD_0+D_0B^\ast)\\
&\phantom{=}\text{}+h^2(D_0F+FD_0)+h^3(D_\perp F+FD_\perp)\\
&\geq\text{$\Delta$}_0+h^2\text{$\Delta$}_\perp+h^4C'-\frac{1}{4}\text{$\Delta$}_0-C'h^2\\
&\phantom{=}\text{}-h^2\left(\text{$\Delta$}_0+C'\right)-h^3\left(\text{$\Delta$}_\perp+C'\right)\\
&\geq\frac{1}{2}\text{$\Delta$}_0+\frac{1}{2}h^2\text{$\Delta$}_\perp-Ch^2
\end{align*}
for some $C>0$ and all $h$ small enough.
head: environment

label: e:<Delta0 omegai,omegai> to 0
title: Proof
body_md:
In the case $k=1$, 
\eqref{e:asymptotics of eigenforms}
just means
$\left\langle\text{$\Delta$}_{h_i}\omega_i,\omega_i\right\rangle\to0$.
Therefore
$$
\left\langle\left(\frac{1}{2}\text{$\Delta$}_0+\frac{1}{2}h_i^2\text{$\Delta$}_\perp-Ch_i^2\right)\omega_i,\omega_i\right\rangle\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
$$
by Proposition~\ref{p:Delta h}. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{e:<Delta0 omegai,omegai> to 0}
\langle\text{$\Delta$}_0\omega_i,\omega_i\rangle\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
\end{equation}
and $\langle\text{$\Delta$}_\perp\omega_i,\omega_i\rangle$ is uniformly bounded since both
$\text{$\Delta$}_0$ and $\text{$\Delta$}_\perp$ are positive operators. It follows that
$\omega_i$ is uniformly bounded in $W^1\Omega$. Therefore some subsequence of
$\omega_i$ is weakly convergent in $W^1\Omega$ (and thus strongly convergent in
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$) to some $\omega\in W^1\Omega$. From \eqref{e:<Delta0 omegai,omegai> to 0} we also
get that $\|D_0\omega_i\|\to0$. So 
$D_0\omega_i\to0$ strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$, yielding
$\omega\in\ker{\mathbf D}_0$ because ${\mathbf D}_0$ is a closed operator in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$. But $\ker{\mathbf D}_0=L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$ by
\eqref{e:L2calH1}. Thus the result follows for $k=1$.

For $k=2$, it follows from \eqref{e:asymptotics of eigenforms} that 
$$\left\|d_{h_i}\omega_i\right\|\in o(h_i)\;,\quad
\left\|\delta_{h_i}\omega_i\right\|\in o(h_i)\;,$$
yielding that 
$$
\left(\frac{1}{h_i}d_{0,1}+d_{1,0}+h_id_{2,-1}\right)\omega_i
\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
\left(\frac{1}{h_i}\delta_{0,-1}+\delta_{-1,0}+h_i\delta_{-2,1}\right)\omega_i
\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,
$$
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ by \eqref{e:dh} and \eqref{e:deltah}. Hence
$$
\Pi\left(d_{1,0}+h_id_{2,-1}\right)\omega_i
\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
\Pi\left(\delta_{-1,0}+h_i\delta_{-2,1}\right)\omega_i
\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
$$ 
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ as well, and thus so does the sequence
$\Pi D_\perp\omega_i$. Then 
$$
D_1\Pi\omega_i=\Pi D_\perp\Pi\omega_i
=\Pi D_\perp\omega_i-\Pi D_\perp\widetilde\Pi\omega_i\text{$\longrightarrow$}0
$$
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ by Lemma~\ref{l:H1}-(i). It follows that $\omega\in\ker{\mathbf D}_1$
because ${\mathbf D}_1$ is a closed operator in $L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$. But $\ker{\mathbf D}_1=\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2$ by Theorem~\ref{t:H1}-(iii), and the
result follows for $k=2$.

For the case $k>2$, we can assume $\omega_i\in\Omega^r$ and 
$\omega\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_2^{u,v}$ for some integers $u+v=r$. Let
$\omega_i^a=\pi_{a,r-a}\omega_i$ for each integer $a$, and set
$$
\omega_i'=\sum_{a\geq0}h_i^{-a}\omega_i^{u+a}\;,\quad
\omega_i''=\sum_{a\geq0}h_i^{-a}\omega_i^{u-a}\;.
$$
Now, by Theorem~\ref{t:calHk}, the result follows from the following claim.

\begin{claim}\label{claim:omega'}
For $0<a<k$, we have 
$$\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d\omega_i'\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,\quad
\pi_{u-a,v+a-1}\delta\omega_i''\text{$\longrightarrow$}0\;,$$
strongly in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$.
\end{claim}

Clearly 
$$\pi_{u,v+1}d\omega_i'=d_{0,1}\omega_i^u\;,\quad
\pi_{u,v-1}\delta\omega_i''=\delta_{0,-1}\omega_i^u\;.$$
Thus both of these components converge strongly to zero because $\omega\in L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1$. 

To prove Claim~\ref{claim:omega'} for other bihomogeneous components observe
that, again from \eqref{e:asymptotics of eigenforms}, both 
$\left\|d_{h_i}\omega_i\right\|$ and $\left\|\delta_{h_i}\omega_i\right\|$ are
in $o\left(h_i^{k-1}\right)$.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{e:omega'}
\left\|h_i^2d_{2,-1}\omega_i^{b-2}+h_id_{1,0}\omega_i^{b-1}
+d_{0,1}\omega_i^b\right\|
\in o\left(h_i^{k-1}\right)\;,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{e:omega''}
\left\|h_i^2\delta_{-2,1}\omega_i^{b+2}+h_i\delta_{-1,0}\omega_i^{b+1}
+\delta_{0,-1}\omega_i^b\right\|
\in o\left(h_i^{k-1}\right)\;,
\end{equation}
for every integer $b$, by considering bihomogeneous components of 
$d_{h_i}\omega_i$ and $\delta_{h_i}\omega_i$. Now 
\begin{align*}
\pi_{u+1,v}d\omega_i'&=d_{1,0}\omega_i^u+h_i^{-1}d_{0,1}\omega_i^{u+1}\;,\\
\pi_{u-1,v}\delta\omega_i''&=
\delta_{-1,0}\omega_i^u+h_i^{-1}\delta_{0,-1}\omega_i^{u-1}\;.
\end{align*}
Both of these components strongly converge to zero in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ too by 
\eqref{e:omega'} and \eqref{e:omega''}, since so does
$h_id_{2,-1}\omega_i^{u-1}$ and $h_i\delta_{-2,1}\omega_i^{u+1}$ because
$d_{2,-1}$ and $\delta_{-2,1}$ are of order zero and $\|\omega_i\|=1$. 

The other bihomogeneous components of $d\omega_i'$ and $\delta\omega_i''$ are the following ones,
where $a\geq2$,
\begin{align*}
\pi_{u+a,v-a+1}d\omega_i'&=h_i^{-a+2}d_{2,-1}\omega_i^{u+a-2}+h_i^{-a+1}d_{1,0}\omega_i^{u+a-1}
+h_i^{-a}d_{0,1}\omega_i^{u+a}\;,\\
\pi_{u-a,v+a-1}\delta\omega_i''&=
h_i^{-a+2}\delta_{-2,1}\omega_i^{u-a+2}+h_i^{-a+1}\delta_{-1,0}\omega_i^{u-a+1}
+h_i^{-a}\delta_{0,-1}\omega_i^{u-a}\;,
\end{align*}
which strongly converge to zero in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ for $a<k$ by
\eqref{e:omega'} and \eqref{e:omega''}. This finishes the proof of
Claim~\ref{claim:omega'}.

title: Proof
body_md:
First, we can assume the metric is bundle-like by \eqref{e:N'rh}. So we can apply the results
of this section.

If we had a strict inequality ``$<$'' in~\eqref{e:small eigenvalues k} for some
$k\geq2$, by the isomorphism $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_k^r\cong E_k^r$ there are sequences $\omega_i\in\Omega^r$ and
$h_i\downarrow0$ such that $\|\omega_i\|=1$, $\omega_i\perp\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_k$, and
$$\langle\text{$\Delta$}_{h_i}\omega_i,\omega_i\rangle\in O(h_i^{2k})\;.$$
But then we get a contradiction by Theorem~\ref{mt:asymptotics of eigenforms}. So inequality ``$\geq$''
holds in~\eqref{e:small eigenvalues k} for all $k\geq2$.

The proof of ``$\geq$'' in \eqref{e:small eigenvalues 1}  follows with the same arguments since
$\widehat E_1^r\cong\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^r$, which is of finite dimension if and only if so is $ L^2\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^r$.

For $k\geq2$, inequality ``$\leq$'' of
\eqref{e:small eigenvalues k} in Theorem~\ref{mt:small eigenvalues} follows directly from 
Corollary~\ref{c:bfEkr Hausdorff of finite dim} and Theorem~\ref{t:Ek=bfEk}, as was pointed out in Remark~\ref{r:leq}.

Now observe that, for each $h>0$ and each $\omega\in\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^r$, we have 
$$D_h\omega=hD_\perp\omega+h^2F\omega\;,$$
according to \eqref{e:D h}. Therefore the inequality ``$\leq$'' in \eqref{e:small eigenvalues 1} 
follows from the isomorphism $\text{$\mathcal{H}$}_1^r\cong\widehat E_1^r$ by using the well known variational formula
$N_h^r(\lambda)=\sup_V\dim V$, where $V$ runs over the subspaces of $\Omega^r$ satisfying
$$\langle\text{$\Delta$}_h\omega,\omega\rangle\leq\lambda\,\|\omega\|^2$$
for all $\omega\in V$.
